excerpts.author: luca_zanolini
excerpts.content:
Yes. 

I confirmed it by removing the fix (deleting the and had_no_participation conjunct from the credit condition so process_attestation reverts to the original will_set_new_flag-only behavior) rebuilding the pyspec, and running the test.

 It fails on the unpatched spec with:
assert 64000000000 == 32000000000

With the fix restored, the test passes.

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content:
because the setup is as follows:

Deathstar recognizes it will propose twice in a row, say N and N+1. You also hold keys for an active builder. 

1) Takes a bid from your own builder with a trustless payment. 
2) attest to your block. 
3) Withhold the payload
4) The next proposer introduces a slashable attestation for the same block with wrong target.

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: you don't care about the impact, you just check if it causes a consensus split
